assessments.title: A declared string 400, but validation writes problem+json
assessments.why: The specification declares 400 as a string (application/json or text/plain), while the generated ValidationFilter writes application/problem+json - a media type the operation does not declare. The client reads its title as the string; the field errors are only in Content.
assessments.proposal: Done: the server generator warns (ATC_API_SRV002) - declare the 400 as ValidationProblemDetails to keep the field errors typed. Still open: validation could honour the declared 400 and write the message as the declared string (Atc.Rest.MinimalApi's ValidationFilter).

assessments.title: errorResponseFormat: Custom reading our host's ProblemDetails
assessments.why: Custom exists for a third-party API whose server writes its own error model (the Monta sample). Against our generated server, which writes ProblemDetails for undeclared statuses, the custom model cannot hold type/title/detail/instance; they stay in Content.
assessments.proposal: None: the configuration chose the custom model. For an API served by this generator, ProblemDetails is the format to choose.

assessments.title: errorResponseFormat: PlainTextOnly reading a validation 400
assessments.why: PlainTextOnly reads every undeclared status as a string - also a validation 400, whose title becomes the string and whose field errors are only in Content.
assessments.proposal: None: the configuration chose strings. PlainText (the default) keeps the validation 400 typed.

assessments.title: A foreign body (a proxy, a gateway, another server)
assessments.why: The body does not come from the generated server - an HTML error page, XML, a JSON string, invalid JSON or another vendor's JSON. No generated type can hold it: the typed fields stay null and the text is kept in Content (for every media type with the Atc.Rest.Client error-body fix).
assessments.proposal: None: this is the best a client can do with that body.

assessments.title: errorResponseFormat: Custom reading our host's ProblemDetails
assessments.why: Custom exists for a third-party API whose server writes its own error model (the Monta sample). Against our generated server, which writes ProblemDetails for undeclared statuses, the custom model cannot hold type/title/detail/instance; they stay in Content.
assessments.proposal: None: the configuration chose the custom model. For an API served by this generator, ProblemDetails is the format to choose.

assessments.title: errorResponseFormat: PlainTextOnly reading a validation 400
assessments.why: PlainTextOnly reads every undeclared status as a string - also a validation 400, whose title becomes the string and whose field errors are only in Content.
assessments.proposal: None: the configuration chose strings. PlainText (the default) keeps the validation 400 typed.

assessments.title: A foreign body (a proxy, a gateway, another server)
assessments.why: The body does not come from the generated server - an HTML error page, XML, a JSON string, invalid JSON or another vendor's JSON. No generated type can hold it: the typed fields stay null and the text is kept in Content (for every media type with the Atc.Rest.Client error-body fix).
assessments.proposal: None: this is the best a client can do with that body.

assessments.title: errorResponseFormat: Custom reading our host's ProblemDetails
assessments.why: Custom exists for a third-party API whose server writes its own error model (the Monta sample). Against our generated server, which writes ProblemDetails for undeclared statuses, the custom model cannot hold type/title/detail/instance; they stay in Content.
assessments.proposal: None: the configuration chose the custom model. For an API served by this generator, ProblemDetails is the format to choose.

assessments.title: errorResponseFormat: PlainTextOnly reading a validation 400
assessments.why: PlainTextOnly reads every undeclared status as a string - also a validation 400, whose title becomes the string and whose field errors are only in Content.
assessments.proposal: None: the configuration chose strings. PlainText (the default) keeps the validation 400 typed.

assessments.title: A foreign body (a proxy, a gateway, another server)
assessments.why: The body does not come from the generated server - an HTML error page, XML, a JSON string, invalid JSON or another vendor's JSON. No generated type can hold it: the typed fields stay null and the text is kept in Content (for every media type with the Atc.Rest.Client error-body fix).
assessments.proposal: None: this is the best a client can do with that body.

assessments.title: A declared string 400, but validation writes problem+json
assessments.why: The specification declares 400 as a string (application/json or text/plain), while the generated ValidationFilter writes application/problem+json - a media type the operation does not declare. The client reads its title as the string; the field errors are only in Content.
assessments.proposal: Done: the server generator warns (ATC_API_SRV002) - declare the 400 as ValidationProblemDetails to keep the field errors typed. Still open: validation could honour the declared 400 and write the message as the declared string (Atc.Rest.MinimalApi's ValidationFilter).

assessments.title: errorResponseFormat: Custom reading our host's ProblemDetails
assessments.why: Custom exists for a third-party API whose server writes its own error model (the Monta sample). Against our generated server, which writes ProblemDetails for undeclared statuses, the custom model cannot hold type/title/detail/instance; they stay in Content.
assessments.proposal: None: the configuration chose the custom model. For an API served by this generator, ProblemDetails is the format to choose.

assessments.title: errorResponseFormat: PlainTextOnly reading a validation 400
assessments.why: PlainTextOnly reads every undeclared status as a string - also a validation 400, whose title becomes the string and whose field errors are only in Content.
assessments.proposal: None: the configuration chose strings. PlainText (the default) keeps the validation 400 typed.

assessments.title: A foreign body (a proxy, a gateway, another server)
assessments.why: The body does not come from the generated server - an HTML error page, XML, a JSON string, invalid JSON or another vendor's JSON. No generated type can hold it: the typed fields stay null and the text is kept in Content (for every media type with the Atc.Rest.Client error-body fix).
assessments.proposal: None: this is the best a client can do with that body.

errorBodies: Validation exceptions thrown by handler code (the feature matrix runs one).

The Development environment beyond one exception per host: the matrices run as Production, and Production_A5xxFromAnException_CarriesNothingOfIt_AndDevelopmentNamesIt checks that a Production 5xx carries nothing of the exception on either host and that Development names it.
Network failures, timeouts and cancellation (the feature matrix runs a reset, a hang, a stall and a mid-body cancel).

HEAD, and 2xx statuses other than 200 and 204 on the sweep operations (every 1xx, 2xx and 3xx has its own operation under Statuses 1xx-3xx; a HEAD answered 200 and 404 with the GET's headers and no body is read by every client in TypedClient_Head_ReturnsNoValue_AndReadsNoBody, OperationClient_Head_IsItsStatus_WithoutAValue and the TypeScript HEAD gate).

What only OpenAPI 3.1 / 3.2 can say, beyond the request-binding matrix's 3.1 body (type arrays, null on the wire, a const, a tuple): every matrix also runs from its specification as a 3.1 document, which says what the 3.0 one says; the Feature support tab compiles the 3.1 and 3.2 scenarios.
The React Query / SWR hooks, Zod runtime validation, date conversion and naming strategies: the error path is the same `ApiError`.
A browser runtime: the TypeScript clients run on Node, so CORS and header exposure are not observed.
Node's fetch rejects every 407 response, so the Fetch client cannot be observed on 407.

Node's fetch resends a request answered 421 on a reused connection on a new one (the Fetch standard), and now and then fails the resent body (UND_ERR_REQ_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH, about 2 in 100 against Kestrel): the harness makes such a call again, three times at most, and a Fetch cell that fails all three is platform.
bodyMedia: Real PDFs or images: the files are synthetic bytes (every byte value) under the media types.
A browser's default XHR adapter for Axios: Node's http adapter and the fetch adapter are run.
Uploads other than PDF and PNG.
A streamed download in the other clients beyond its bytes (the streamed C# EndpointPerOperation result is checked for its bytes; the probe buffers them).
requestBinding: Cookies from a browser: a page cannot set the Cookie header; the TypeScript cells run on Node.
guard: A real JWT in the matrix: its bearer handler reads a plain-text token that spells out subject, scopes and roles (GeneratedPolicies_ReadScopesAndRolesFromARealJwt runs the generated scope and role checks against signed JWTs read by AddJwtBearer).
A limiter partitioned by IP: every client runs on one machine, so the limited operations partition by user.
feature: A browser runtime: the React Query and SWR hooks render with React on jsdom in Node.
The hooks on a 304: a browser cache sends the condition, not a hook.
A cancelled SWR read: SWR hands its fetcher no signal (a hook's timeout of the caller's own is run, through the client's fetch option).
enumCasing: An integer enum: it is a number on the wire, so there is no casing.
A dictionary keyed by an enum: OpenAPI 3.0 has no enum-typed property names.
The C# member name of a value whose wire form is no C# name (OutOfStock for out-of-stock): that is the marker's readEnumMemberNames, not casing.
validation: The MapEndpoints() host: it has no validation filter, so a generated model or parameter is not validated there (the wiki says so; a test pins it).
multipleOf, uniqueItems, minProperties / maxProperties and const: the generator emits no attribute for them.
An array in the path, a header or a cookie: the matrix sends arrays in the query and the bodies.
An empty string or an empty array where the wire cannot tell it from no value (the query, a header, a cookie, a form field).
A format: uri path parameter: ASP.NET Core keeps %2F encoded in a route value, so a URL in one path segment does not arrive as it was sent.
Compare, Remote, ValidateNever, CreditCard and Phone: MVC and DataAnnotations attributes with no OpenAPI keyword to generate them from (a phone number is a pattern here).

A request body that is a bare primitive, a dictionary or untyped JSON: it stays [FromBody], so a value that does not convert is the framework's 400 that names nothing (a model, a oneOf, a list and a webhook payload are read by the generated reader).
validationCombined: An XML body, a query, a header or a cookie: FluentValidation sees the bound model or parameters record however it arrived, and the Validation matrix covers the DataAnnotations of every place a value arrives.
A validator with a scoped dependency (a DbContext): the generated AddApiValidatorsFromDomain() registers validators as singletons; the wiki shows how to resolve a scoped service per call.
FluentValidation's own options (cascade modes, rule sets, severity): the validator decides; the server only collects its errors.
A validator registered for the list itself (List<T>, with RuleForEach): Atc.Rest.MinimalApi's own tests cover it - the matrix registers what a domain writes, the model's validator.

readiness:
Atc REST 3.0 readiness

State of feature/error-body-3.0 (generator), 24 October 2026.

  • Atc.Rest.MinimalApi 3.0.0 is released on nuget.org, then 3.0.1 (dependency updates), 3.1.0 on 16 October (a form endpoint's request is validated as a JSON body of the same model, and the unused Scalar dependency is gone) and 3.1.1 (each item of a list body is validated by the model's FluentValidation validator, and an XML request's messages name a field by its XML name). The tests and the samples use 3.1.1, which is now the minimum (ATC_API_DEP013).
  • Atc.Rest.Client is released up to 2.7.0, with every library issue this branch raised. 2.7.0 is the minimum for the EndpointPerOperation client and the TypedClient's Result style (ATC_API_DEP011).
  • The generator 3.0 is not released. The branch and the wiki are committed locally and not pushed yet.

The numbers on this page come from the run that wrote it: the verdicts per matrix on the Overview tab, the compile gate and the diagnostics on Feature support, and the Showcase apps under Playwright. The commit the run was made from is in the page header. These notes are written by hand, so they carry no counts - a test checks that, so editing this page alone can turn a run red. A Playwright run that started before that commit is marked stale rather than shown as this commit's.

Decisions

#DecisionStatus
1Release Atc.Rest.MinimalApi 3.0.0? released 3.0.0 is on nuget.org. The report run on the released package showed no cell different from the run on the branch it was built from. 3.0.1, 3.1.0 and 3.1.1 followed, and every test project and sample now uses 3.1.1.
2The validation 400 against a declared 400 body. The ValidationFilter always answers an invalid request with a ValidationProblemDetails, even where the specification declares its own 400 body. done
  • A declared ProblemDetails 400 is read as the ValidationProblemDetails subtype. The generated ValidationProblemDetails derives from ProblemDetails, so the field errors stay typed.
  • A declared model or string 400 keeps its type, and the field errors are only in Content. Documented, with the hint ATC_API_SRV002.
3What belongs in Atc.Rest.Client, not in generated workarounds. released in 2.1.0 - 2.7.0
  • Error bodies of every media type are read as text; binary responses keep an error's content type, headers and typed error (2.1.0).
  • Trim- and Native AOT-ready requests: URL-encoded forms, a body with its own media type, repeated multipart fields and a JSON part, URI-escaped query keys (2.2.0, 2.3.0).
  • Streamed responses read by the library in five formats (StreamFraming), with typed errors and headers, record and error-body limits, and the default error registrations (2.4.0, 2.5.0).
  • Server-Sent Events with their event state: the last event id for a resume, in the EndpointPerOperation client and the TypedClient's Result style (2.6.0).
  • A request body sent as a stream of records (JSON Lines, JSON Text Sequences) by the request builder, and an empty text answer read as the empty text (2.7.0).
The generated code uses the library for each and keeps no workaround for them.
4Release the generator 3.0? open Waiting for the branch and the wiki to be pushed, the review with the coworkers, and their approval. Until then the work continues on this branch.

Since the 5 October notes

  • Server.
    • A factory for an error status that declares a model takes the model; a result factory takes the headers its response declares.
    • Every server gets the one-call host wiring (Add{Api}Api() / Map{Api}Api()), also without Atc.Rest.MinimalApi.
    • Validation messages name the value as it was sent; a server without the ValidationFilter still rejects a missing required parameter or property.
    • The parameters build and bind through the Request Delegate Generator, and the JSON writes are trim- and Native AOT-ready (ATC_API_AOT001 for what still binds by reflection).
  • Parameters and bodies. Objects in the query (deepObject, form with explode), arrays in the path and headers, a JSON part of a multipart form, a oneOf part, charset-aware text bodies, HEAD and OPTIONS operations, and new diagnostics for what cannot be bound or sent (ATC_API_OPR037, OPR038, OPR040).
  • Streaming.
    • Server-Sent Events, JSON Lines, JSON arrays, JSON Text Sequences and multipart/mixed are read the same way in every client, including what other servers put between records.
    • A streamed EndpointPerOperation operation has its own result class with typed errors and declared headers.
    • x-sse-item-events names the events that carry items.
    • An event stream can be resumed: the server sets each event's id, every client gives the last id back.
  • SignalR hubs (x-signalr-hubs). The server gets the hub contract and the C# clients a typed hub client; hubs declare methods beside events; the TypeScript client reads hubs with the same parser and its React hook connects to the hub on the server, reconnects after a close and is StrictMode-safe.
  • TypeScript. Every SignalR hub compiles, Zod schemas carry a default written next to a $ref, and the clients read bodies by their charset.
  • Tooling. Overlays from the CLI options file; the CLI cannot hang on a tool it runs; one rule names the root namespace for the server, the handlers and the client.
  • Report. Every matrix also runs from its specification as an OpenAPI 3.1 document; the feature matrix covers the stream formats on the wire, a resumed event stream and SignalR hubs; the Changes tab keeps the run history.
  • Showcase. Live streams in every format with a drop and a resume, a live price feed with a heartbeat, a replay buffer and fan-out, and the notifications hub generated from the specification in all three apps.
  • From a consumer's migration.
    • A streamed response sends its status and headers before its first item, in every format.
    • The clients follow Retry-After on a 503 as on a 429; x-retry-total-timeout-seconds bounds the attempts as a whole; AddApiResilience() takes the document's policy as its default.
    • Every EndpointPerOperation result has Problem and ValidationProblem; an optional operation parameter is = null; the build reports System.Enum on an extensible enum (ATC_API_CLT003).
    • A rule about the specification can be switched off where it does not fit (x-atc-suppress, an .editorconfig section for the specification file, suppressRules); ATC_API_NAM005 accepts one casing used throughout the document.
    • Constants for the cache tags; the Location and header wrappers give the wrapped result's status and value; a hub's payload models stay in the shared namespace.

Fixed in the 5 October round

  • Every status below 400. 2xx and 300 write their declared body, 205 and 304 none, the redirects write Location, a 1xx gets no factory (ATC_API_OPR030); the C# client never reads a 3xx as an error; TypeScript has the arms notModified and redirection.
  • TypeScript naming. A naming strategy that differs from the API's casing renames the wire too (helpers/wireNames.ts).
  • Error bodies. String accessors give a problem's message; XML and binary error bodies reach Content; a declared error model reads a body of another shape leniently; Fetch and Axios read success and error bodies by one rule.
  • Models and enums. Properties are written under their exact spec names; a server string enum is a string in every host; the clients' enums are extensible (extensibleEnums: false keeps the classic enum). A string enum whose values are not its member names (rtsp, in-progress) was written by v2 as the member name, so a v2 and a v3 peer refuse each other's JSON bodies; readEnumMemberNames: true in the marker reads both during a rollout.
  • OpenAPI Overlays in the build and the CLI.
  • A broken specification is reported, never a crash (a fuzz test over every scenario).

Known limitations (documented)

  • HttpClient.Timeout (100 s) caps a long per-operation retry timeout (Working with Resilience). A long-lived stream is fine on the client's one HttpClient: every timeout ends at the response headers (Working with C# Client).
  • The build finds multi-part specs by the {Base}_{Part}.yaml convention only.
  • Node's fetch rejects every 407 response, so the Fetch client cannot be observed on 407 in Node. Browsers behave differently; this is a platform limit, not a client one.
  • The framework's event-stream writer has no comment line, so a server heartbeat is a named event that the clients read past.
  • A SignalR event whose name is no C# identifier cannot be a method of the typed hub client interface; the server sends it with the generated contract's Send…Async.
  • Not exercised by the matrix: the How it was tested tab lists everything the E2E run does not cover.

What 3.0 changes

The complete list, with a fix for each break, is the wiki page Upgrading to v3 (Upgrading-to-v3.md in the local wiki repository until it is pushed).

Release sequence once we agree

  1. Push the generator branch and the wiki.
  2. Review with the coworkers. (Atc.Rest.MinimalApi 3.1.1 and Atc.Rest.Client 2.7.0: done, released and in use.)
  3. Merge the generator branch and release 3.0.
review:
Scope: this review covers the error-body matrix only (the Error bodies tab and its MapEndpoints() and OpenAPI 3.1 variants), as it stood on 2026-10-04. The other matrices (Body media, Request binding, Security & rate limiting, Features, Enum casing) are not part of it; each has its own verdict test that proves a wrong result fails.

The rules and the data were checked by five independent reviewers. Each started with no context from the session that built the harness, and each worked from the wiki (the documented contract), the code and the JSON alone.

ReviewMethodResultWhat changed because of it
1. Blind reproduction 28 cells across every client and group. For each, the reviewer derived the expected result from the wiki, the spec and the wire body before looking at the cell. 28 of 28 agree; no verdict disagreements. One inaccurate wiki sentence fixed: TypeScript named arms exist only for 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 429.
2. Rules against the docs Read every verdict rule next to the wiki statement it enforces, looking for branches that could never fail. 18 findings, among them rules that could never fail and two contradictions between the docs and the code.
  • Every rule was rewritten: accessor, type and arm come from the spec, and values are compared field by field.
  • Two contradictions: the C# string accessor over a ProblemDetails is fixed in the product; the validation 400 against a declared 400 body is decision 2 on the readiness tab.
3. Coverage gaps Listed what the matrix does not exercise, or exercises without being able to fail. 7 gap areas.
  • Added to the matrix:
    • a model under application/problem+json;
    • a $ref to components/responses;
    • the exception → status mapping;
    • Retry-After on every 429;
    • the undeclared-status Content check;
    • TypeScript type, title, detail and instance;
    • a stub with foreign bodies;
    • provenance of the uncommitted tree.
  • Three product bugs found by reading code were each reproduced by a failing test, then fixed: the TypedClient Result download body, Axios and Fetch on non-JSON bodies, and C# on non-text bodies.
  • Everything else is listed under Not exercised.
4. Final review The same three angles (rule soundness, blind reproduction, lossy groups), plus the product changes of this round. 55 cells derived blind: 52 agree, 3 agree only by assuming the implementation (now documented), 1 disagreed with a wiki page. The report's legend and three method claims were overstated. The JSON was older than the rule code.
  • Two product bugs, each reproduced by a new matrix case before the fix:
    • a declared-model accessor threw on a foreign body (stubs now also run on a declared-model route);
    • Axios parsed a JSON-string error twice (a "42" stub).
  • The wiki now states that client-added statuses are ProblemDetails in every format but Custom; Marker-Files and Working-with-Security contradicted the code.
  • Documented that a declared model fills only the shared fields; a body without a Content-Type is not affected.
  • The rest of the exception mapping was added to the matrix.
  • The negative control was widened to every rule, and a charset test was added.
  • The legend and the method text were corrected, and the report was regenerated from a fresh build with a working-tree hash.
5. Every HttpStatusCode A fresh reviewer for the statuses below 400 and the validation-400 change: product correctness against RFC 9110 and ASP.NET Core, rule soundness, blind reproduction, docs.
  • Provenance is exact: the report's stash tree equals the working tree.
  • 16 of 16 blind cells agree.
  • The product changes are correct against RFC 9110 and ASP.NET Core.
  • Findings: a redirect factory taking a string let a v2 X(message) call compile into a redirect to the message; the redirect cells only proved platform redirect-following; a redirect declared before 200 lost the 200's TypeScript type; a text body on a redirect gave wrong metadata; the 1xx wire text was inaccurate; two doc caveats.
  • Redirect factories now take a Uri, so old calls fail at compile time.
  • New test Redirects_NotFollowed_AreTheirOwnAccessors checks the generated Is… accessors with auto-redirect off.
  • TypeScript redirect arms are added after the declared 2xx, and redirection is in the union.
  • Metadata no longer advertises a body on a redirect.
  • The 1xx wire text now states what happened.
  • 422 is pinned to UnprocessableEntity.
  • The Upgrading rows cover text-bodied factories and the ValidationProblemDetails type-test order.

Negative control

The test MatrixVerdicts_FailRegressedResults feeds every verdict rule a correct result, which must pass, and one regressed result per failure mode, which must fail. The regressions it covers:

  • a changed or lost value, or a JSON string where a message belongs;
  • a wrong custom-model field;
  • the default body on the status's own accessor;
  • an undeclared status without its raw Content;
  • a wrong TypeScript arm, a missing named arm in the generated union, or a wrong detail;
  • a wrong default body on the wire, or a 5xx detail outside Development;
  • a missing Retry-After on a 429;
  • a handler value missing from its ProblemDetails;
  • a lost XML body in C#;
  • a stub wire mismatch;
  • a parsed model on a TypedClient Result error.

Bugs the matrix found, now fixed (each reproduced by a failing test first)

  • C#, a declared error model over a foreign body. The accessor threw InvalidContentAccessException; it now reads the body leniently.
  • TypeScript Axios, a JSON-string error body. It was parsed twice: "42" became a number.
  • C#, a declared string or text status with no body from the handler. The accessor gave the host wiring's ProblemDetails as JSON text; it now gives its message.
  • C#, application/xml / application/octet-stream error bodies. Content and the typed accessors were empty, because Atc.Rest.Client keeps such bodies as bytes. The generated client now reads them as text.
  • C# TypedClient, Result style. A download's error body was not in Content.
  • TypeScript Axios. Kept application/octet-stream and untyped error bodies as the body.
  • TypeScript Fetch. Dropped XML error bodies, although it reads XML success bodies as text.
